title: Driver leaderboard with ties
context: Rank drivers by completed bookings; equal bookings share a rank.
task: Return driver_id, bookings (2 decimals) and rank_position using RANK() over bookings descending.
hint: Aggregate then RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(fare) DESC).
answer: SELECT driver_id, ROUND(SUM(fare), 2) AS bookings, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(fare) DESC) AS rank_position FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id;

title: Each rider's most recent ride
context: Support sees the last trip on the rider's profile.
task: Return rider_id, ride_id and ride_date for each rider's latest ride (ties by highest ride_id).
hint: ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY rider_id ORDER BY ride_date DESC, ride_id DESC.
answer: SELECT rider_id, ride_id, ride_date FROM (SELECT rider_id, ride_id, ride_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rider_id ORDER BY ride_date DESC, ride_id DESC) AS rn FROM rides) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Time between a rider's rides
context: Ride frequency drives retention.
task: Return rider_id, ride_id and gap_days = days since the rider's previous ride (integer), only where a previous ride exists.
hint: LAG(ride_date) OVER (PARTITION BY rider_id ORDER BY ride_date, ride_id).
answer: SELECT rider_id, ride_id, gap_days FROM (SELECT rider_id, ride_id, CAST(julianday(ride_date) - julianday(LAG(ride_date) OVER (PARTITION BY rider_id ORDER BY ride_date, ride_id)) AS INTEGER) AS gap_days FROM rides) WHERE gap_days IS NOT NULL;

title: Cumulative bookings by day
context: Month-to-date bookings curve.
task: Return ride_date, bookings (that day's completed fare, 2 decimals) and cumulative (running sum, 2 decimals), ordered by date.
hint: SUM() OVER (ORDER BY ride_date).
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT ride_date, SUM(fare) AS bookings FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY ride_date) SELECT ride_date, ROUND(bookings, 2) AS bookings, ROUND(SUM(bookings) OVER (ORDER BY ride_date), 2) AS cumulative FROM d;

title: 7-day rolling ride count
context: Smooth the daily volume line.
task: Return ride_date, rides (that day) and rolling7 (average over the current and 6 preceding rows, 2 decimals), ordered by date.
hint: ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT ride_date, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides GROUP BY ride_date) SELECT ride_date, rides, ROUND(AVG(rides) OVER (ORDER BY ride_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS rolling7 FROM d;

title: Driver earnings quartiles
context: Segment the fleet by completed bookings.
task: Return driver_id, bookings (2 decimals) and quartile = NTILE(4) ordered by bookings descending (1 = top).
hint: CTE then NTILE.
answer: WITH b AS (SELECT driver_id, SUM(fare) AS bookings FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id) SELECT driver_id, ROUND(bookings, 2) AS bookings, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY bookings DESC) AS quartile FROM b;

title: Driver share of city bookings
context: Concentration risk per market.
task: Return city, driver_id and pct_of_city (1 decimal) = driver bookings / city bookings * 100, completed rides only.
hint: SUM(bookings) OVER (PARTITION BY city).
answer: WITH b AS (SELECT d.city, r.driver_id, SUM(r.fare) AS bookings FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY r.driver_id) SELECT city, driver_id, ROUND(bookings * 100.0 / SUM(bookings) OVER (PARTITION BY city), 1) AS pct_of_city FROM b;

title: Surge by hour of day
context: When does surge kick in?
task: Return pickup_hour, rides and surge_share_pct = rides with surge > 1 / rides * 100 (1 decimal), ordered by hour.
hint: GROUP BY hour with conditional AVG.
answer: SELECT CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS pickup_hour, COUNT(*) AS rides, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN surge_multiplier > 1 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS surge_share_pct FROM rides GROUP BY pickup_hour ORDER BY pickup_hour;

title: Does surge raise cancellations?
context: Compare rider-cancel rate on surge vs non-surge requests.
task: Return surge_flag ('surge' if surge_multiplier > 1 else 'normal') and rider_cancel_pct (1 decimal).
hint: CASE in GROUP BY and in AVG.
answer: SELECT CASE WHEN surge_multiplier > 1 THEN 'surge' ELSE 'normal' END AS surge_flag, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled_by_rider' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS rider_cancel_pct FROM rides GROUP BY surge_flag;

title: Surge premium earned per driver
context: Extra fare attributable to surge = fare − fare / surge_multiplier.
task: Return driver_id and surge_premium (2 decimals) = SUM(fare - fare / surge_multiplier) over completed rides, for drivers with premium > 0.
hint: Arithmetic inside SUM, HAVING > 0.
answer: SELECT driver_id, ROUND(SUM(fare - fare / surge_multiplier), 2) AS surge_premium FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id HAVING SUM(fare - fare / surge_multiplier) > 0;

title: Rider retention: second ride within 30 days
context: What share of riders come back within a month of their first ride?
task: Return signup_month (YYYY-MM of signup_date) and repeat_30_pct (1 decimal) = riders with a 2nd completed ride within 30 days of their first / riders with at least one completed ride.
hint: First ride per rider, then EXISTS for another ride in the window.
answer: WITH f AS (SELECT rider_id, MIN(ride_date) AS first_ride FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY rider_id) SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', ri.signup_date) AS signup_month, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rides r WHERE r.rider_id = f.rider_id AND r.status = 'completed' AND r.ride_date > f.first_ride AND julianday(r.ride_date) - julianday(f.first_ride) <= 30) THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS repeat_30_pct FROM f JOIN riders ri ON ri.rider_id = f.rider_id GROUP BY signup_month;

title: Monthly active riders and churn
context: Riders active in month m but not in m+1.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM), active = distinct riders that month, churned = of those, riders with no ride the next calendar month; ordered by month. Exclude the last month.
hint: Distinct (rider, month); LEFT JOIN to next month.
answer: WITH rm AS (SELECT DISTINCT rider_id, strftime('%Y-%m', ride_date) AS month FROM rides) SELECT a.month, COUNT(*) AS active, SUM(CASE WHEN b.rider_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS churned FROM rm a LEFT JOIN rm b ON b.rider_id = a.rider_id AND b.month = strftime('%Y-%m', date(a.month || '-01', '+1 month')) WHERE a.month < (SELECT MAX(month) FROM rm) GROUP BY a.month ORDER BY a.month;

title: Longest streak of consecutive shift days
context: Reliability: most consecutive days a driver was online.
task: Return driver_id and longest_streak (max run of consecutive shift_date values).
hint: date(d, -ROW_NUMBER) grouping trick per driver.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT driver_id, shift_date FROM driver_shifts), g AS (SELECT driver_id, shift_date, date(shift_date, '-' || ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY driver_id ORDER BY shift_date) || ' days') AS grp FROM d), s AS (SELECT driver_id, COUNT(*) AS streak FROM g GROUP BY driver_id, grp) SELECT driver_id, MAX(streak) AS longest_streak FROM s GROUP BY driver_id;

title: Idle hours per shift
context: Hours online minus ride time on that date.
task: Return shift_id, driver_id, shift_date and idle_hours (2 decimals) = hours_online − (sum of duration_min of completed rides that day) / 60, only where idle_hours > 0.
hint: LEFT JOIN rides on driver + date; COALESCE the sum.
answer: SELECT s.shift_id, s.driver_id, s.shift_date, ROUND(s.hours_online - COALESCE(SUM(r.duration_min), 0) / 60.0, 2) AS idle_hours FROM driver_shifts s LEFT JOIN rides r ON r.driver_id = s.driver_id AND r.ride_date = s.shift_date AND r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY s.shift_id HAVING s.hours_online - COALESCE(SUM(r.duration_min), 0) / 60.0 > 0;

title: City supply vs demand by month
context: Hours online vs completed rides per city per month.
task: Return city, month, hours (1 decimal), rides and rides_per_hour (2 decimals). Aggregate shifts and rides separately by (city, month).
hint: Two CTEs keyed on city+month, joined.
answer: WITH h AS (SELECT d.city, strftime('%Y-%m', s.shift_date) AS month, SUM(s.hours_online) AS hours FROM driver_shifts s JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = s.driver_id GROUP BY d.city, month), r AS (SELECT d.city, strftime('%Y-%m', r.ride_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.city, month) SELECT h.city, h.month, ROUND(h.hours, 1) AS hours, COALESCE(r.rides, 0) AS rides, ROUND(COALESCE(r.rides, 0) / h.hours, 2) AS rides_per_hour FROM h LEFT JOIN r ON r.city = h.city AND r.month = h.month;

title: Rating drift per driver
context: Average stars on a driver's last 5 rated rides vs their first 5.
task: Return driver_id, early_avg and late_avg (2 decimals) for drivers with 10+ ratings, where late_avg < early_avg.
hint: ROW_NUMBER asc and desc per driver over rated rides.
answer: WITH r AS (SELECT rd.driver_id, rr.stars, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rd.driver_id ORDER BY rd.ride_date, rd.ride_id) AS rn_a, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rd.driver_id ORDER BY rd.ride_date DESC, rd.ride_id DESC) AS rn_d, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY rd.driver_id) AS n FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides rd ON rd.ride_id = rr.ride_id) SELECT driver_id, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN rn_a <= 5 THEN stars END), 2) AS early_avg, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN rn_d <= 5 THEN stars END), 2) AS late_avg FROM r WHERE n >= 10 GROUP BY driver_id HAVING late_avg < early_avg;

title: Stored rating vs computed rating
context: drivers.rating should track the average of ride ratings.
task: Return driver_id, rating (stored), computed (2 decimals, AVG(stars)) and diff (2 decimals, stored − computed) where ABS(diff) > 0.3.
hint: Join an aggregate of ride_ratings.
answer: WITH c AS (SELECT r.driver_id, AVG(rr.stars) AS computed FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides r ON r.ride_id = rr.ride_id GROUP BY r.driver_id) SELECT d.driver_id, d.rating, ROUND(c.computed, 2) AS computed, ROUND(d.rating - c.computed, 2) AS diff FROM drivers d JOIN c ON c.driver_id = d.driver_id WHERE ABS(d.rating - c.computed) > 0.3;

title: Median completed fare per city
context: Averages are skewed by long airport trips.
task: Return city and median_fare (2 decimals) over completed rides.
hint: ROW_NUMBER and COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY city).
answer: WITH f AS (SELECT d.city, r.fare, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.city ORDER BY r.fare) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY d.city) AS cnt FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'completed') SELECT city, ROUND(AVG(fare), 2) AS median_fare FROM f WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2) GROUP BY city;

title: Slowest 10% of rides
context: Speed outliers point to traffic or fraud.
task: Return ride_id and speed_kmh (1 decimal) for completed rides in the bottom 10% by speed (PERCENT_RANK <= 0.1), distance_km > 0.
hint: Compute speed in a CTE, PERCENT_RANK over it.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT ride_id, distance_km / (duration_min / 60.0) AS speed FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' AND distance_km > 0 AND duration_min > 0) SELECT ride_id, ROUND(speed, 1) AS speed_kmh FROM (SELECT *, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY speed) AS pr FROM s) WHERE pr <= 0.1;

title: Rides by city × status
context: Wide funnel table per city.
task: Return city (driver's), completed, cancelled_by_rider, cancelled_by_driver and no_show counts.
hint: One conditional SUM per column.
answer: SELECT d.city, SUM(CASE WHEN r.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed, SUM(CASE WHEN r.status = 'cancelled_by_rider' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_by_rider, SUM(CASE WHEN r.status = 'cancelled_by_driver' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_by_driver, SUM(CASE WHEN r.status = 'no_show' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_show FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id GROUP BY d.city;

title: Hourly heatmap row: rides per hour bucket per city
context: Four time buckets as columns.
task: Return city and morning (05–11), afternoon (12–16), evening (17–21), night (22–04) ride counts.
hint: CASE on the pickup hour inside SUM.
answer: WITH h AS (SELECT d.city, CAST(SUBSTR(r.pickup_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS hr FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id) SELECT city, SUM(CASE WHEN hr BETWEEN 5 AND 11 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS morning, SUM(CASE WHEN hr BETWEEN 12 AND 16 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS afternoon, SUM(CASE WHEN hr BETWEEN 17 AND 21 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS evening, SUM(CASE WHEN hr >= 22 OR hr <= 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS night FROM h GROUP BY city;

title: Rides per week including empty weeks
context: The weekly chart must show zero-ride weeks.
task: Using a recursive CTE starting at '2025-01-06' (a Monday) stepping 7 days until '2025-07-28', return week_start and rides = rides with ride_date in [week_start, week_start + 6], ordered by week_start.
hint: LEFT JOIN rides on a date range.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE w(week_start) AS (SELECT '2025-01-06' UNION ALL SELECT date(week_start, '+7 days') FROM w WHERE week_start < '2025-07-28') SELECT w.week_start, COUNT(r.ride_id) AS rides FROM w LEFT JOIN rides r ON r.ride_date >= w.week_start AND r.ride_date <= date(w.week_start, '+6 days') GROUP BY w.week_start ORDER BY w.week_start;

title: Rider–driver pairs who met 3+ times
context: Repeat matches suggest favourites (or collusion).
task: Return rider_id, driver_id and trips = completed rides together, for pairs with 3 or more.
hint: GROUP BY both ids, HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3.
answer: SELECT rider_id, driver_id, COUNT(*) AS trips FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY rider_id, driver_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

title: Drivers who served riders from every city
context: Cross-market drivers.
task: Return driver_id for drivers whose completed rides cover every distinct rider city.
hint: COUNT(DISTINCT rider city) = total distinct rider cities.
answer: SELECT r.driver_id FROM rides r JOIN riders ri ON ri.rider_id = r.rider_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY r.driver_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ri.city) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) FROM riders);

title: Second-busiest hour per city
context: The runner-up demand hour.
task: Return city, pickup_hour and rides for the hour ranked 2nd by rides in each city (DENSE_RANK = 2; ties by hour).
hint: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY rides DESC).
answer: WITH h AS (SELECT d.city, CAST(SUBSTR(r.pickup_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS pickup_hour, COUNT(*) AS rides FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id GROUP BY d.city, pickup_hour) SELECT city, pickup_hour, rides FROM (SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY rides DESC) AS rk FROM h) WHERE rk = 2;

title: Suspiciously fast rides
context: Speed over 80 km/h inside a city is implausible.
task: Return ride_id, driver_id, distance_km, duration_min and speed_kmh (1 decimal) where speed > 80 for completed rides.
hint: Compute speed and filter.
answer: SELECT ride_id, driver_id, distance_km, duration_min, ROUND(distance_km / (duration_min / 60.0), 1) AS speed_kmh FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' AND duration_min > 0 AND distance_km / (duration_min / 60.0) > 80;

title: Drivers with abnormal tip ratios
context: Tips above 40% of fare on 2+ rides.
task: Return driver_id and big_tip_rides = number of rated rides where tip > 0.4 × fare, for drivers with 2 or more.
hint: Join and compare tip to fare.
answer: SELECT r.driver_id, COUNT(*) AS big_tip_rides FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides r ON r.ride_id = rr.ride_id WHERE rr.tip > 0.4 * r.fare GROUP BY r.driver_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

title: Bookings, tips and hours without fan-out
context: Three one-to-many tables per driver — one row per driver, correct totals.
task: Return driver_id, bookings (2 dp), tips and hours (1 dp) for every driver in drivers (0 where none).
hint: Aggregate each table in its own CTE, LEFT JOIN from drivers.
answer: WITH b AS (SELECT driver_id, SUM(fare) AS bookings FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY driver_id), t AS (SELECT r.driver_id, SUM(rr.tip) AS tips FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides r ON r.ride_id = rr.ride_id GROUP BY r.driver_id), h AS (SELECT driver_id, SUM(hours_online) AS hours FROM driver_shifts GROUP BY driver_id) SELECT d.driver_id, ROUND(COALESCE(b.bookings, 0), 2) AS bookings, COALESCE(t.tips, 0) AS tips, ROUND(COALESCE(h.hours, 0), 1) AS hours FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN b ON b.driver_id = d.driver_id LEFT JOIN t ON t.driver_id = d.driver_id LEFT JOIN h ON h.driver_id = d.driver_id;

title: Back-to-back rides
context: Rides where the same driver's next ride started within 20 minutes on the same day.
task: Return ride_id, driver_id, next_ride_id where the next ride (by date, pickup_time) is on the same date and the pickup gap is ≤ 20 minutes.
hint: LEAD over (date, time); minutes = hh*60+mm.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT ride_id, driver_id, ride_date, CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time,1,2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time,4,2) AS INTEGER) AS mins, LEAD(ride_id) OVER (PARTITION BY driver_id ORDER BY ride_date, pickup_time) AS next_ride_id, LEAD(ride_date) OVER (PARTITION BY driver_id ORDER BY ride_date, pickup_time) AS next_date, LEAD(CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time,1,2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(pickup_time,4,2) AS INTEGER)) OVER (PARTITION BY driver_id ORDER BY ride_date, pickup_time) AS next_mins FROM rides) SELECT ride_id, driver_id, next_ride_id FROM s WHERE next_date = ride_date AND next_mins - mins <= 20;

title: Riders driving 50% of bookings
context: How concentrated is demand?
task: Return rider_id and bookings (2 dp) for the riders whose cumulative completed fare (descending, ties by rider_id) reaches 50% of total — include the rider that crosses 50%.
hint: Running SUM with ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING compared to 0.5 × total.
answer: WITH b AS (SELECT rider_id, SUM(fare) AS bookings FROM rides WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY rider_id), c AS (SELECT rider_id, bookings, SUM(bookings) OVER (ORDER BY bookings DESC, rider_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS prev_cum, SUM(bookings) OVER () AS total FROM b) SELECT rider_id, ROUND(bookings, 2) AS bookings FROM c WHERE COALESCE(prev_cum, 0) < 0.5 * total;

title: Drivers whose every rated ride was 5 stars
context: Perfect records (min 3 ratings).
task: Return driver_id and ratings count for drivers with 3+ ratings where every rating is 5.
hint: HAVING MIN(stars) = 5 AND COUNT(*) >= 3.
answer: SELECT r.driver_id, COUNT(*) AS ratings FROM ride_ratings rr JOIN rides r ON r.ride_id = rr.ride_id GROUP BY r.driver_id HAVING MIN(rr.stars) = 5 AND COUNT(*) >= 3;

title: Take rate sensitivity
context: If the platform take moved from 25% to 30%, how much more revenue per city?
task: Return city and delta (2 dp) = 0.05 × completed fare per driver city.
hint: SUM(fare) * 0.05.
answer: SELECT d.city, ROUND(SUM(r.fare) * 0.05, 2) AS delta FROM rides r JOIN drivers d ON d.driver_id = r.driver_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.city;

title: Cumulative unique riders by month
context: How the rider base compounds.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM) and cumulative_riders = distinct riders whose first ride (any status) is on or before that month, for every month with rides, ordered by month.
hint: First-ride month per rider, then a correlated count.
answer: WITH f AS (SELECT rider_id, strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(ride_date)) AS first_month FROM rides GROUP BY rider_id), m AS (SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', ride_date) AS month FROM rides) SELECT m.month, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM f WHERE f.first_month <= m.month) AS cumulative_riders FROM m ORDER BY m.month;
